A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FOSSA method and ZEDD benchmark. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching renumbered appendix material.

before.justification: v1 reports original FOSSA evaluations, robustness experiments and ablations in Tables 2–5 and Fig. 5, alongside original ZEDD data collection and analysis.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds Infinigen ablation results, timing measurements, additional ZEDD metrics and MobileDepth qualitative evaluations.

M1.justification: The stack attention, focus-distance embedding, feature collapse, refinement, decoder and synthetic-training procedure remain unchanged. Section 3.3 newly specifies the SiLog parameter λ = 0.5; this is additional documentation, with no evidence of a changed objective or training procedure.

E1.justification: New Appendix A3 evaluates MobileDepth phone-captured focus stacks qualitatively, with four examples in Fig. A6. v1 only discussed that dataset. Existing training and evaluation datasets remain; extending ablations to the already evaluated Infinigen dataset adds no new dataset coverage.

E2.justification: The corresponding quantitative comparisons retain their baseline methods. MobileDepth uses existing DFF-DFV, DFF-FV and HybridDepth baselines, while Fig. A9 visualizes methods already evaluated on ZEDD in Table 2. Newly discussed DDFS is not evaluated.

E3.justification: Table 2 adds MAE, MSE and RMSE for ZEDD and removes δ1.15 reporting for both ZEDD and Infinigen. Table 5 adds timing measurements under a stated single-L40, 700 × 512 setup. Existing splits, training budgets and robustness settings are retained.

E4.justification: Table 5 extends the seven existing architectural and domain-randomization ablations from ZEDD to Infinigen, checking whether the same design conclusions hold there. It also adds timing alongside existing computational-cost measurements. The ablated components and Fig. 5 robustness sweeps remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests for model performance. The added results continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice; Fig. 5 concerns variation across capture settings, not statistical uncertainty.

E6.justification: Shared numerical entries in Tables 2–5 remain unchanged. Newly reported ZEDD MAE/MSE/RMSE for ViT-S are 0.370/0.661/0.534; Table 5 adds Infinigen ablation scores and timing, including 51.9 ms for the full ViT-S model. Table 2 removes δ1.15 entries, and Figs. A6/A9 add qualitative results. These extend the evidence without demonstrating a revised model's performance gain.

T1.justification: The problem formulation, circle-of-confusion equations, generalized PSF and its special cases, and focus-distance sampling mathematics remain unchanged. No theorem, proof or derivation is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the ZEDD benchmark, FOSSA architecture, synthetic-training contribution and generalization claims, including the stated 55.7% ZEDD and 40.4% DDFF error reductions. The added definition of zero-shot clarifies the existing scope.

C2.justification: Section 5.3 newly qualifies monocular comparisons as contextual positioning, disclaiming direct head-to-head or replacement claims. Section 5.5 interprets consistent ZEDD/Infinigen ablations as evidence against dataset-specific tuning. The static-scene and simulation-to-real limitations are retained.

D1.justification: v2 discloses SiLog λ = 0.5, two-day training on four 48-GB L40 GPUs, and the single-L40 setup for Table 5. Conversely, Section 5.3 removes v1's explicit DAv2 Hypersim-indoor and KITTI-outdoor checkpoint choices. Code/data release statements and the remaining appendix implementation details are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2.1 adds DDFS and contrasts its camera-setting modeling with FOSSA's focus-distance embeddings and randomized training. It corrects DEReD from fully supervised to fully self-supervised. References to Moeller's variational reconstruction and Pertuz's focus-measure analysis are removed; the broader positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: There are localized prose revisions, an explicit zero-shot definition and typo corrections. New Appendix A3 shifts the existing training, evaluation and limitations sections to A4–A6. The main section order and most narrative remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Tables 2 and 5 are reformatted for additional metric, dataset and timing columns. New Figs. A6 and A9 show MobileDepth and expanded ZEDD comparisons. Existing PSF and full-stack visualizations become A7 and A8, with local appendix reflow rather than wholesale visual restructuring.

improvement.justification: The Infinigen ablations check whether design conclusions transfer beyond ZEDD, while additional error metrics and qualitative examples broaden the evidence. Loss and hardware disclosures and the monocular-comparison qualification improve transparency. Removing the DAv2 checkpoint choices causes a limited reproducibility loss, but the overall benefit is modest and positive; the core method and established results remain unchanged.
